title: Pulsebar & Healthline: compact GPU pool controls and status surface for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, action-oriented status surface (Pulsebar) and an accompanying Healthline detail panel for Redwood Console's Dedicated GPU pools. The goal is to provide a single-row summary that surfaces pool health, current autoscale mode, queued burst credits, and quick actions (pause pool, trigger manual scale, view logs) while also allowing an inline expand to a more detailed Healthline panel with metrics, recent events, and suggested mitigation steps. Focus areas: legibility at small widths, accessibility for keyboard/screen-reader, and predictable placement for on-call workflows.
background: Product and SRE have observed that platform engineers often need a fast way to assess pool health on call and trigger quick mitigations without hunting through multiple screens. Current Dedicated pool pages are too deep for triage. This design proposes a condensed top-level row visible in the pool list and pool detail header, plus an expandable Healthline with richer telemetry (GPU utilization percentiles, kernel stall alerts, KV cache hit rate, burst credits). We consulted with runtime and infra teams about telemetry availability and with PM about permission gating for actions.
acceptance_criteria: Pulsebar present in pool list and pool detail header showing health state, autoscale mode, burst credits, and 3 quick actions
Healthline panel expands inline and includes sparkline of GPU utilization (1m/5m/1h), current batching efficiency, recent autoscale events, and top 3 alerts
Quick actions respect RBAC: action buttons disabled/hidden according to role returned by backend
Keyboard navigable and screen-reader labelled; contrast and touch target sizes meet AA standards
Prototype validated in two 30-minute ops shadow sessions with SRE and two product interviews

decisions: Favor single compact row that appears in both pool list and pool detail header to reduce mental model surface
Show SLA degradation score (0-100) derived by SRE, and map to health colors with explicit tooltip
Quick actions exposed: Pause pool, Force scale (+1 or -1), Open live logs; destructive actions push to modal with confirmation and audit reason
Burst credits shown as numeric value with donut micro-chart; burst auto-enable toggle hidden behind admin RBAC
open_questions: Should Pulsebar be sticky on scroll within pool detail to keep quick actions in view?
What tolerance do we set for alert flapping before muting in the Healthline? (SRE input required)
Do we surface cost delta estimates for an immediate manual scale in the Pulsebar or leave that to the rollouts page?
